page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The hybridisation
lines: In diamond every carbon atom is sp³
Each carbon is joined to four other
carbon atoms and carries no lone pair,
so it needs four hybrid orbitals.
mix to give four sp³ orbitals.
steps.why: Each carbon in diamond has four bonded neighbours and no lone pair, so four hybrid orbitals are needed. Four orbitals can only come from one s orbital and all three p orbitals, which is sp³.
common_mistakes: Answering sp² for diamond. That is the hybridisation in graphite, where each carbon is joined to three others.
Writing that carbon uses only two of its 2p orbitals. All three 2p orbitals are used here, so the hybridisation is sp³.
steps.memory_tip: Four bonded carbon atoms means four orbitals, so sp³.
steps.margin_note: Answer sp³ and say each carbon is joined to four other carbon atoms.

The same pattern repeats in all three
directions, so the whole crystal is one

lines.text: Carbon in diamond is sp³ hybridised

steps.why: Four sp³ orbitals repel one another equally and point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron, which fixes the angle at 109°28′. Because each of the four neighbours is bonded in the same way, the arrangement repeats through the crystal instead of stopping at a molecule.
common_mistakes: Giving the bond angle as 120°. That is the graphite angle; in diamond the angle is 109°28′.
Calling diamond a molecule of carbon atoms. There are no separate molecules; the whole crystal is one covalent network.
steps.memory_tip: sp³ points to a tetrahedron: 109°28′ and a C–C length of 154 pm.
steps.margin_note: The angle and the bond length complete the description of the arrangement.

insider_note: The answer itself is sp³, so a complete answer adds the reason: each carbon is joined to four others at 109°28′ in a tetrahedral pattern that repeats through the crystal.
